record.evidence:
A prefix '%PDF
stream
BT (Hello) ET
endstream
' contains a real text page and no /Page token. Appending '/Page' 200,000 times adds exactly 1,000,000 bytes and makes pdf_page_count_in_text return 200,000. The stream extractor returns one printable page, so the all-pages-nontext rejection is false; normalization then pushes 199,999 empty Strings and prepare_units creates 200,000 PreparedUnit records. The default 100 MB size-only gate permits more than 20 million five-byte markers.
Confirmed `m` and `n` originate in old/new prepared PDF unit vectors and the DP allocation is exactly `(m+1)*(n+1)` machine words followed by nested reverse loops.

record.method: Candidate-local static cardinality/data-flow analysis from PDF bytes through page inference, unit construction, incremental mapping, and the index byte-size gate.
evidence: `pdf_page_count_in_text` counts raw `/Page` substrings at deterministic.rs:421-437 without a syntax tree or limit.
`pdf_text_pages` pads with empty strings until `page_count` at prepare.rs:315-347; one printable page makes the all-garbage rejection false.
`prepare_units` creates one PreparedUnit per inferred page at prepare.rs:125-164.
`lcs_fingerprint_pairs` allocates `vec![vec![0usize; n+1]; m+1]` and fills every cell at prepare.rs:387-416.
The CLI enforces only `candidate.size_bytes <= max_input_bytes` at main.rs:9047-9061, so a compact marker-heavy file remains admissible.
record.proof_gap: No OOM stress case was executed against the immutable target. The allocation cardinalities and attacker control of N are explicit in the reviewed code.

record.method: Static target-blob complexity and reachability validation with concrete allocation arithmetic.
evidence: pdf_page_count_in_text returns the count of attacker-controlled raw /Page substrings.
pdf_text_pages pads to that count; prepare_units creates the same number of PreparedUnit records when at least one page has plausible extracted text.
The second index resolves a prior normalized instance and calls map_units before incremental/full mode selection.
For 10,000 old and 10,000 new units, the DP cells alone require about 800 MB for 64-bit usize values, excluding Vec and unit overhead.
counterevidence: A no-text PDF returns no units, so the crafted file must include one plausible text-layer page; raw PDF syntax makes this straightforward.
The default 100 MB file cap bounds bytes but not /Page token count and permits orders of magnitude more units than needed for OOM.

record.method: static target-blob source-to-sink and allocation-size validation
record.evidence: A printable first stream passes the PDF text gate while empty pages are padded to the spoofed count. Two 50,000-unit revisions request about 2.5 billion usize cells, approximately 20 GB before row overhead.

record.title: Quadratic full-matrix LCS exhausts memory on PDF revisions
record.evidence: Static inspection confirmed (m+1)*(n+1) usize allocation and O(m*n) loops before incremental threshold evaluation, with no cardinality-product cap.
Inferred page count pads both unit lists; 50,000 squared usize cells exceed 18 GiB before row-vector overhead.

record.counterevidence: The byte-size gate limits the source file and a PDF with no plausible text layer exits early. Neither condition caps marker-derived page cardinality once any plausible extracted page is present, and the incremental mapper has no size cutoff.
record.evidence: The derived usize count is used without an upper bound in linear allocation loops, and the incremental path has explicit O(m*n) storage and work.
record.proof_gap: No crafted file or runtime stress test was produced, per task constraints.

record.method: immutable static call-chain and exact allocation calculation
record.evidence: One printable stream plus N /Page markers survives the all-pages-nontext check and pads to N units. At m=n=20,000 the DP owns 400,040,001 usize cells (~3.20 GB before Vec overhead) and performs 400,000,000 cell updates.
record.proof_gap: No live exhaustion run was performed; parent validation can reproduce under disposable memory/time limits.

attack_path_facts.title: incremental unit mapping allocates a quadratic LCS matrix
attack_steps: A lower-trust contributor supplies an indexed document revision with many prepared units and later supplies another large revision.
Incremental indexing passes the old and new unit lists to map_units.
The LCS implementation allocates and fills an (m+1) by (n+1) usize matrix without a unit-count or work budget.
The allocation reaches hundreds of megabytes or gigabytes at feasible derived unit counts and can repeatedly terminate or wedge indexing while the crafted revisions remain.
assumptions: A local content contributor can control successive revisions in a scope the operator reindexes.
Both old and new prepared representations contain sufficiently many units.
The incremental mapping path is reached.
attack_path_facts.context: The lower-trust revision source is in scope and the full matrix is allocated before any similarity shortcut can help. Derived unit amplification can make the required cardinality practical under existing byte limits.
attack_path_facts.exposure: Operator-mediated local revision/index workflow; no network or listener is required.
attack_path_facts.identity: The contributor controls document revisions; the KCS user bears the allocation and indexing failure.
preconditions: Two indexed revisions must each generate a large unit list.
The operator must run incremental index or reindex.
Unit cardinality must be high enough to exceed available memory or acceptable work.
attack_path_facts.attacker_control: yes: an in-scope local content contributor controls both revision contents and therefore both matrix dimensions
attack_path_facts.category: quadratic algorithmic complexity and persistent local denial of service
mitigations: Raw input size is capped elsewhere.
Fingerprint matches may reduce later work, but not matrix allocation.
attack_path_facts.auth_scope: untrusted local document revisions processed by an operator command
attack_path_facts.impact_surface: memory/CPU availability and incremental indexing liveness
attack_path_facts.target_reach: the KCS process handling the crafted scope/revisions
counterevidence: The path requires two large revisions and incremental mapping rather than a single ordinary small file.
Large failure cases were computed rather than allocated.
No confidentiality, authorization, or cross-scope integrity effect is shown.
blindspots: The minimum document size and unit-generation pattern needed for a reliable host-specific denial are not fully measured.
Interaction with operating-system memory limits is environment-dependent.
attack_path_facts.rationale: A realistic lower-trust revision source can drive both dimensions of an unbounded quadratic matrix and persistently deny indexing. High availability impact with the multi-revision/operator/cardinality prerequisites gives Medium likelihood, mapping to Medium/P2.
